frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The dimming/failing of light such that clear seeing lapses — the fading of illumination toward darkness. Concretely realized either in the sky (the darkening end of the daylight span, dusk/nightfall) or in the eye (dimmed, failing sight). The root marks the low-light pole where perceptual clarity is diminished, as opposed to the bright/rising pole.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The dimming/failing of light such that clear seeing lapses — the fading of illumination toward darkness. Concretely realized either in the sky (the darkening end of the daylight span, dusk/nightfall) or in the eye (dimmed, failing sight). The root marks the low-light pole where perceptual clarity is diminished, as opposed to the bright/rising pole.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Thirteen of the fourteen occurrences are the temporal nouns ʿishāʾ / ʿashiyy / ʿashiyya, all denoting the dimming, darkening portion of the day — dusk, evening, nightfall. 12:16:3:1 "wa-jāʾū abāhum ʿishāʾan yabkūn" = they came to their father AT NIGHTFALL; 24:58:27:2 "min baʿdi ṣalāti l-ʿishāʾ" = after the ʿishāʾ (night/dark) prayer; 79:46:7:1 "lam yalbathū illā ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā" = they tarried only an EVENING or its forenoon. A large sense-family pairs al-ʿashiyy with an explicit morning/rising term, framing it as the DIMMING counterpart to brightening light: 18:28 & 6:52 "bi-l-ghadāti wa-l-ʿashiyy" (dawn/morning ↔ evening), 3:41 & 40:55 "bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ibkār" (evening ↔ early-morning), 38:18 "bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ishrāq" (evening ↔ sunrise-shining), 19:11 & 19:62 "bukratan wa-ʿashiyyan" (early-day ↔ evening), 40:46 "ghuduwwan wa-ʿashiyyan" (morning ↔ evening), 30:18 "wa-ʿashiyyan wa-ḥīna tuẓhirūn" (evening, and noon). 38:31:4:3 "ʿuriḍa ʿalayhi bi-l-ʿashiyyi l-ṣāfināt" = the horses were displayed to him in the (declining-light) late-day. Across all of these the root supplies the same thing: the low-light, dimming phase — never the bright/rising phase, which is always carried by a DIFFERENT root standing opposite it. The single verb, 43:36:2:1 "wa-man yaʿshu ʿan dhikri l-raḥmān" = whoever is DIM-SIGHTED toward / turns a blind eye from the remembrance of the Merciful, exposes the more abstract core: yaʿshu is dimmed/failing vision (night-blindness). Subtracting the ʿan-construction (which adds the "away-from" vector) leaves exactly "dimness of sight" — the eye-internal analogue of the sky-external dusk. The concrete image shared by all fourteen is thus failing light and the loss of clear seeing that accompanies it.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: Form N (11×) is a time-noun/verbal-noun realization — it specializes the root's "dimming of light" as a NAMED PART OF THE DAY (dusk/evening/nightfall). Form T (tag on 19:11, 19:62; the ʿashiyyan variant) is the same nominal sense, indefinite accusative adverbial ("[at] evening"). Form V (43:36 yaʿshu) realizes the root as a process/state verb = "to be dim-sighted." Once form is subtracted, the noun's "evening" and the verb's "dim sight" reduce to one residue: diminished light → diminished seeing. CONSTRUCTION: the prepositional frames bi-/wa- + al-ʿashiyy supply "at/in [the time]"; the pairing prepositions with morning-terms (ghadāt, bukra, ibkār, ishrāq, ghuduww) supply the CONTRAST that pins the root to the dark pole. In 43:36 the "ʿan" supplies the "turning-away-from" vector; the root itself contributes only the dimness/blindness, not the avoidance. PARTICIPANTS/CONTEXT: worship-timing (3:41, 6:52, 18:28, 19:11, 38:18, 40:55), eschatological punishment-timing (40:46, 79:46), narrative arrival (12:16), Solomon's horses (38:31), legal privacy (24:58) — all context; strip them and the invariant "the dim end of light / dimmed sight" remains.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 43:36:2:1 "wa-man yaʿshu ʿan dhikri l-raḥmān" is the hardest, because it is the sole non-temporal, non-nominal occurrence and reads as "turns away from remembrance," which superficially looks like avoidance/aversion rather than "evening." It reconciles cleanly once form and construction are subtracted: yaʿshu is the verb "to have dim/failing vision" (night-blindness); the ʿan adds the directional "away-from." The residue "dimness of sight" is the eye-internal mirror of the sky-external "dimness of light (dusk)" carried by the nouns. The internally-attested bridge is that both are the SAME concrete event — light failing so that clear perception lapses — which is exactly the invariant the nominal cluster already forces. Rather than breaking the unity, 43:36 is what proves the root's core is "dimming of light-for-seeing" and not merely the calendar-slot "evening."
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative: the root's core is simply the TEMPORAL slot "evening / late-day / nightfall" (a pure time-of-day meaning), with no perceptual component. This covers 13 of 14 occurrences effortlessly. Internal evidence arbitrates decisively against it: 43:36 (yaʿshu ʿan) is not temporal at all and cannot be derived from "evening-time" — it requires a perceptual sense (dim/failing sight). A single abstraction, "dimming of light such that seeing fails," subsumes both the 13 temporal nouns and the 1 perceptual verb, whereas "evening-time" leaves 43:36 unaccounted. Therefore the temporal reading is a form-specific (time-noun) specialization of the deeper residue, not the residue itself. The consistent opposition of al-ʿashiyy to morning/rising terms further confirms the residue is specifically the DIMMING (falling-light) direction, not a neutral time-label.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: (1) l-y-l (layl, "night") and gh-s-q (ghasaq, "onset/thickening of darkness") name established/full darkness — ع ش و names the TRANSITION/dimming phase (dusk, the light failing) rather than achieved night. (2) The paired morning-roots gh-d-w / b-k-r / sh-r-q ("dawn, early-morning, shining") are its systematic OPPOSITES throughout the data (six explicit pairings), marking the rising/brightening pole; ع ش و is exclusively the falling/dimming pole. (3) ʿ-m-y (ʿamā, "total blindness") denotes complete loss of sight — ع ش و's yaʿshu is PARTIAL, light-dependent dimness of vision (night-blindness), not total blindness. Falsifiability condition: the hypothesis fails if any occurrence used the root for (a) a bright/rising/high-noon time, (b) full/settled darkness with no sense of transition, or (c) total, light-independent blindness. No such occurrence appears; every one of the 14 sits on the failing-light / dimmed-seeing pole.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — "the dimming/failing of light such that clear seeing lapses" — is recoverable in every one of the 14 occurrences after subtracting form, construction, participants, and context. The 13 nominal occurrences are surface-transparent as the dimming end of the daylight span (dusk/evening/nightfall), and their repeated explicit pairing with morning/rising roots (ghadāt, bukra, ibkār, ishrāq, ghuduww) fixes the direction determinately at the falling-light pole. The lone verb (43:36, yaʿshu ʿan) is not forced into the "evening" mold; instead it independently exposes the abstraction (dim/failing sight) that the nouns already imply, via the internally-motivated bridge that dusk and night-blindness are one event — light failing so perception dims. This makes the unity robust rather than stipulated: the hardest case strengthens rather than threatens it. The direction is determinate and the contribution is sharply distinct from neighbor roots for full night (layl/ghasaq), morning (ghadw/bukr/shurūq), and total blindness (ʿamā). The only inferential step is generalizing the perceptual sense from a single verb token, but that step is well-anchored by the shared concrete image, so I judge STRONG rather than MODERATE. No occurrence remains unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Refutation sweep of all 14 accounted for. 13 temporal nouns (ʿishāʾ/ʿashiyy/ʿashiyya) all denote the dimming, darkening end of the daylight span (dusk/evening/nightfall): 12:16 arrival at nightfall, 24:58 the dark ʿishāʾ prayer, 79:46 evening vs forenoon, 38:31 late-day horse display, plus eight merism pairings (18:28/6:52 ghadāt↔ʿashiyy; 19:11/19:62 bukra↔ʿashiyy; 40:46 ghuduww↔ʿashiyy; 3:41/40:55 ʿashiyy↔ibkār; 38:18 ʿashiyy↔ishrāq; 30:18 ʿashiyy+noon). The single verb 43:36 yaʿshu ʿan dhikr = dim/failing sight is the eye-internal analogue.

Hardest case = 43:36 (the verb): I pressed the homonymy objection (evening-time vs dim-sight as two roots) and the alternate "turns a blind eye / averse" reading. It resolves non-circularly: classical lexicon roots both al-aʿshā/ʿashā (weak, night-blind sight) and al-ʿashiyy (evening) in a shared 'dimness' notion, and even the 'averse' gloss derives from the dim-sighted-toward-firelight image, so the dimming metaphor survives. Second pressure point = over-breadth via 'perceptual clarity': the time-nouns foreground time, but the candidate's primary axis (fading illumination toward darkness) genuinely holds for evening as the darkening end of day, so it is not smuggled in.

Distinctiveness holds strongly: the corpus systematically assigns the bright/rising pole to a DIFFERENT root (ghadāt/bukra/ghuduww/ibkār/ishrāq) and never to E$w; E$w is the transitional dimming pole, discriminable from full night (layl), absolute darkness (ẓalām), and onset-of-dark (ghasaq). Falsifiable: failure condition = any occurrence carrying the bright/rising sense, black-of-night, or an unrelated sense (e.g. ʿashāʾ=meal); none occur (12:16 is time, not meal). No genuine failing occurrence found; unity is distinct and falsifiable — SUPPORTED.
